# monitor


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

This module runs two kinds of work outside the turn you are typing in. A
folder review reads changes that someone else made to a watched folder
and reports on them at the start of your next turn. The beat runs
scheduled work on a timer, with or without an open session. The beat
section is at the end of the page.

## Folder reviews

A folder watch is a standing request to review changes under a folder.
You ask the agent to watch a folder and give it instructions such as
“check each change for correctness”. Whenever files under that folder
change, a reviewer reads the diff and follows the instructions. The
report appears in your next turn.

The model opens a watch with the shalya `watch` tool:
`watch(target, kind='folder', instructions=..., pattern=...)`. `pattern`
is one string of globs separated by commas or spaces, such as
`*.py,*.md`. A glob matches a file name or a whole posix path. An empty
`pattern` matches every file. The tool stores the watch as a row in the
vault, beside the scheduled page, search and reminder watches.
`list_watches` and `cancel_watch` also see the row.

[`Monitors`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#monitors)
does the reviewing.
[`Monitors.sync`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#monitors.sync)
copies the vault’s folder rows into the session.
[`Monitors.check`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#monitors.check)
calls `sync` first and picks up any folder watch the model opened since
the last check. A host without a vault gives the model no tool to open a
folder watch. Code can open one with
[`Monitors.add`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#monitors.add).

A new folder watch takes a baseline: a snapshot of the folder at that
moment. Only later changes are reviewed. The reviewer receives the
watch’s instructions and the changes. It receives nothing from the
conversation that created the watch. The instructions must say
everything the reviewer needs. `add` refuses a watch with empty
instructions.

Each completed review goes into a queue.
[`Monitors.drain`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#monitors.drain)
empties the queue, and the agent adds the drained reviews to its next
prompt with
[`review_notice`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#review_notice).
The queue holds `PENDING_MAX` reviews and drops the oldest. Each review
is also noted to the user. A review that has text is filed in memory
under the key `folder-review:` plus the watch id. A newer review of the
same folder replaces the older one. The agent runs
[`Monitors.check`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#monitors.check)
in a daemon thread between turns.

## Change detection

[`snapshot`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#snapshot)
records the text of every readable file under the watched folder that
matches the pattern.
[`changed`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#changed)
compares two snapshots and returns the files added, edited or removed.
[`report`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#report)
lists the changed files with their added and removed line counts, then
appends the unified diffs.
[`summarise`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#summarise)
returns a one-line count such as `1 added, 1 edited`. A file larger than
`SNAP_MAX_BYTES` is recorded as its size alone. A change to it shows as
a changed size with no diff.

A folder watch’s settle window is the least time between two reviews of
one folder. Changes that arrive inside the window wait and go into the
next review together. A burst of saves produces one review.
`check(force=True)` ignores the window.

## Reviewer

The reviewer is a read-only sub-agent. It has the session’s read tools
and no write tools. `REVIEW_SP` is its system prompt. Reviews use the
session’s sub-agent step setting. Under `auto`, each review gets
`SUB_MAX_STEPS` (80). A numeric setting gives each review that many
steps, up to `SUB_STEP_CEILING` (400).
[`Monitors`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#monitors)
reads `get_steps` before each review. Without that callback, it uses
`auto`. The budget is passed to the backend as `max_steps`. Urai counts
each approved tool call as one step, including calls in a batch. A quiet
backend gets twice that budget to allow for status calls. A separate
read-tool allowance permits four calls per requested step. The reviewer
cannot edit the watched folder. It describes any fix instead of making
it. Without a backend to run it on, the change is recorded with status
`unreviewed`. A review that raises an error is recorded with status
`error`. The baseline moves forward on every review attempt, including a
failed one. A change is never reviewed twice.

### Monitors.sync

``` python
def sync():
```

*Mirror the host’s folder watches: add new vault rows, drop removed
ones.*

``` python
from ramabana.testing import FakeBackend, MemHost, SPEC
```

The example watches a two-file project that
[`MemHost`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/testing.html#memhost)
holds in memory.
[`FakeBackend`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/testing.html#fakebackend)
replaces the reviewer’s model and answers every question with
`sub answer`. The first check returns an empty list because no files
have changed since `add`. After one file is edited, the check returns
one record. The record holds the summary, the review and the diff.

``` python
h = MemHost({'/proj/a.py': 'def a(): return 1\n', '/proj/notes.md': 'hello\n'})
m = Monitors(h, get_backend=lambda: FakeBackend(SPEC))
w = m.add('/proj', 'Review each change for correctness.')
test_eq(len(w.snap), 2)
test_eq(m.check(), [])

h.write('/proj/a.py', 'def a(): return 2\n')
rec, = m.check()
test_eq((rec['status'], rec['files'], rec['summary']), ('ok', 1, '1 edited'))
test_eq(rec['review'].split('\nstate:')[0], 'sub answer')
assert '-def a(): return 1' in rec['changes'] and '+def a(): return 2' in rec['changes']
```

Folder reviews use the sub-agent step setting. Under `auto`, a review
gets 80 steps. A numeric setting applies to the next review. The
read-tool allowance is four calls per step, not one. This example
exhausts that allowance without calling a model.

``` python
def review_read(index: int): return str(index)

review_backend = FakeBackend(SPEC)
review_host = MemHost({"/proj/a.py": "one"})
review_monitor = Monitors(review_host, get_backend=lambda: review_backend, get_tools=lambda: [review_read])
review_monitor.add("/proj", "Review changes.")
review_host.write("/proj/a.py", "two")
assert review_monitor.check(force=True)[0]["status"] == "ok"
review_tool = review_backend.spawned[-1].tools[0]
assert all(review_tool(i) == str(i) for i in range(80 * 4))
assert review_tool(320) != "320"
review_monitor.get_steps = lambda: 2
review_host.write("/proj/a.py", "three")
assert review_monitor.check(force=True)[0]["status"] == "ok"
review_tool_capped = review_backend.spawned[-1].tools[0]
assert all(review_tool_capped(i) == str(i) for i in range(2 * 4))
assert review_tool_capped(8) != "8"
review_monitor.all()[0].last_status
```

A file added inside the settle window waits. The plain check returns an
empty list, and `force=True` reviews the file. A removed file shows as
removed. Each check queues its record. `drain` returns all queued
records once and empties the queue. The agent calls it before its next
turn.

``` python
h.write('/proj/b.py', 'def b(): pass\n')
test_eq(m.check(), [])
rec, = m.check(force=True)
test_eq((rec['summary'], rec['status']), ('1 added', 'ok'))

del h.files['/proj/notes.md']
test_eq(m.check(force=True)[0]['summary'], '1 removed')
```

``` python
test_eq(len(m.drain()), 3)
test_eq(m.drain(), [])
test_eq(review_notice([]), '')

test_eq(_globs('*.py, *.ipynb'), ['*.py', '*.ipynb'])
test_eq(summarise({'a': ('', 'x'), 'b': ('x', 'y')}), '1 added, 1 edited')
test_fail(lambda: m.add('/proj', '  '))
```

`check(block=False)` returns `None` at once when another check is
running. The default `check()` waits for it. The agent’s background
thread uses the default.

``` python
h.write('/proj/a.py', 'def a(): return 3\n')
m.checking.acquire()
try: test_eq(m.check(block=False), None)
finally: m.checking.release()
test_eq(m.check(force=True)[0]['summary'], '1 edited')
```

The same flow runs through the model’s tools. `VaultLike` stands in for
a vault host. It stores watches as rows and keeps filed notes in a list.
The `watch` tool opens a folder watch. The next check picks it up
through `sync` and takes its baseline. An edit then produces a review
filed under the key `folder-review:w1`. After `cancel_watch`, the next
check removes the watch from
[`Monitors`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#monitors).

``` python
from ramabana.tools import MemoryHost, WatchHost, watch_tools

class VaultLike(MemHost, MemoryHost, WatchHost):
    "A host whose watches table is a list and whose memory is the notes it was handed."
    def __init__(self, files): super().__init__(files); self.rows, self.notes = [], []
    def watch(self, target, action='remind', every='1d', note=None, **params):
        w = dict(id=f'w{len(self.rows)+1}', kind=action, target=target, every=86400, note=note, runs=0, last_status='', **params)
        self.rows.append(w); return w
    def watches(self, due_only=False): return list(self.rows)
    def unwatch(self, wid): self.rows = [r for r in self.rows if r['id'] != wid]; return True
    def poll(self): return {'checked': 0, 'ran': 0, 'results': []}
    def remember(self, text, title=None, tags=(), key=''): self.notes.append((title, key, text)); return dict(doc_id='d1', title=title)
    def memory_search(self, query, limit=8): return []
    def memory_tree(self, document=''): return []
    def memory_read(self, node_id): return {}
    def memory_forget(self, doc_id): return False
    watch_actions = ('url', 'remind', 'web', 'folder')

vh = VaultLike({'/proj/a.py': 'one\n'})
vm = Monitors(vh, get_backend=lambda: FakeBackend(SPEC))
wt = {t.__name__: t for t in watch_tools(vh)}
print(wt['watch']('/proj', kind='folder', instructions='Review each change.'))
test_eq(vm.check(force=True), [])
test_eq([w.id for w in vm.all()], ['w1'])
vh.write('/proj/a.py', 'two\n')
rec, = vm.check(force=True)
test_eq((rec['watch_id'], rec['review'].split('\nstate:')[0]), ('w1', 'sub answer'))
test_eq(vh.notes[-1][:2], ('folder review: proj: 1 edited', 'folder-review:w1'))
wt['cancel_watch']('w1')
test_eq(vm.check(), [])
test_eq(vm.all(), [])
```

    watching folder /proj as w1, every 1d

## The beat

Some work must run on a timer with or without an open session, such as a
nightly job that learns from the day’s sessions. pobblebonk does the
timing. It is a small scheduler that installs one job with the operating
system’s scheduler (cron, launchd or Windows Task Scheduler). It keeps
its schedules, the work they fired and the notes that work left in a
SQLite database.

A schedule is a name, an interval and a callback. The callback runs when
the schedule fires. A beat is one pass over the schedules. It runs every
schedule that has come due. A note is a short title and body that a
callback leaves for the next reader. Several readers can share one
database. Each reader sees each note once.

This module holds the Ramabana side of that arrangement. `on_tick(name)`
registers the callback for a schedule from Python.
[`pob`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#pob) opens
the shared database, or returns `None` when pobblebonk is not installed.
[`beat_notes`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#beat_notes)
returns the notes that a reader has not seen yet.
[`beat_notice`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#beat_notice)
wraps them in a `<beat>` block, which the agent adds to its next prompt.
[`beat_notes`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#beat_notes)
reads under the reader name `POB_READER` by default. A session reads
under `POB_READER` plus a colon and its session id.
[`beat_join`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#beat_join)
starts the session’s reader at the newest note. Every open session
therefore sees every note made after it began. Packages that define
recurring work own their schedules. Ramabana runs them.

### on_tick

``` python
def on_tick(
    name
):
```

*Register the callback a fire of schedule `name` runs.*

[`tick`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#tick) is
the `ramabana-tick` command. Run without options, it registers the
callbacks, runs one beat, prints how many schedules ran of those that
fired (`N ran of M fired`, unless `--quiet`) and exits. With no
schedules registered it does nothing and exits with status 0.
`--install` schedules `ramabana-tick --quiet` in pobblebonk to run every
`--every` seconds. `--uninstall` removes it.
[`beat_command`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#beat_command)
builds that command line and quotes the path for the platform’s shell.
[`heartbeat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#heartbeat)
returns the pobblebonk scheduler module, or `None`.

launchd and cron start a job on `/usr/bin:/bin`. That `PATH` holds
neither `claude` in `~/.local/bin` nor Homebrew’s `git-lfs`. Off
Windows,
[`beat_command`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#beat_command)
runs the beat through `/usr/bin/env` with the `PATH` of the shell that
installed it. `--install` prints that `PATH`. The beat carries only
`PATH`. A key exported in a shell profile does not reach the beat. After
you install a tool in a new folder, run `ramabana-tick --install` again
to make the beat find it.

`--install` warns on stderr when its `PATH` is the launchd default, or
when it cannot find one of `BEAT_TOOLS` (`claude`, `git`, `git-lfs`) or
the `ramabana-tick` it schedules. The warning names what is missing
([`beat_missing`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#beat_missing)).
A `claude` that starts with `#!/usr/bin/env node` also needs `node` on
that `PATH`. `--install` still installs. The warning tells you to run it
again from a terminal whose shell finds the missing items.

[`beat_problems`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#beat_problems)
reads the launcher that the scheduler runs. It reports four problems,
each with the command that fixes it. The problems are a launcher written
before the `PATH` was carried, a tool that this shell finds and the
launcher’s `PATH` does not, a `ramabana-tick` that is gone, and a
`beat.env` that other users can read. A session adds these lines to its
first beat note. `ramabana-tick --check` prints them and exits with
status 1 when there are any.

Never put keys in the launcher. Any user can read it. Put keys in
`beat.env` beside `config.toml` (`~/.config/ramabana/beat.env`), one
`NAME=value` per line, and run `chmod 600` on it. Each beat loads
`beat.env` with python-dotenv before any schedule runs. It sets only the
names that its environment lacks. It refuses a file that other users can
read. The `api_key_env` setting in `config.toml` names a variable, and
`beat.env` supplies its value. An `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in `beat.env`
makes Claude Code bill the API instead of the subscription.

launchd starts no second beat while one runs. A hung fire stops every
schedule. A beat stops itself after `--limit` seconds. When `--limit` is
0, `BEAT_LIMIT` applies (six hours). Every schedule in that beat shares
the limit. Off Windows, a SIGALRM raises
[`BeatTimeout`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#beattimeout)
in the running fire. The SIGTERM that launchd sends when it replaces the
job does the same. pobblebonk records the exception as that fire’s
failure, and the beat claims no further fire. A watchdog thread ends the
process a minute later if the fire is stuck where no signal reaches. On
Windows the watchdog is the only bound. `--install --limit N` writes the
limit into the launcher. Task Scheduler on Windows gives a job the
user’s environment. The Windows command therefore does not carry `PATH`.

An installed package registers a callback through a `ramabana.ticks`
entry point (`TICK_GROUP`). The entry point’s name is the schedule’s
name and its value is the callback. The beat imports the package only
when that schedule fires. A slow or broken package costs nothing until
then. A package that fails to import fails that one fire. pobblebonk
retries the fire or leaves a note. An
[`on_tick`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#on_tick)
callback with the same name replaces the entry point’s callback. A
schedule named in `LEARNING_TICKS` (`dhrona`) does nothing while
learning is off and leaves the note `learning is off`. Dhrona registers
its nightly job this way:

``` toml
[project.entry-points."ramabana.ticks"]
dhrona = "dhrona.improve:nightly"
```

### tick

``` python
def tick(
    db:str='', # the shared database; pobblebonk's own by default
    quiet:bool=False, # say nothing on success
    install:bool=False, # schedule this command instead of running one beat
    uninstall:bool=False, # stop the scheduled beat
    every:int=60, # seconds between installed beats, whole minutes
    limit:int=0, # seconds a beat may run before it stops itself; `BEAT_LIMIT` when 0
    check:bool=False, # say what is wrong with the installed beat
):
```

*One beat: run the schedules that are due and leave what they found as
notes.*

*`exe --quiet` as the launcher’s shell reads it, quoted; off Windows it

``` python
if sys.platform != 'win32':
    assert beat_command('/a b/ramabana-tick', path="/x y/bin:/it's/$HOME:/usr/bin") == "/usr/bin/env PATH='/x y/bin:/it'\"'\"'s/$HOME:/usr/bin' '/a b/ramabana-tick' --quiet"
    assert beat_command('/x/ramabana-tick', path='') == '/x/ramabana-tick --quiet'
    test_eq(beat_command('/x/ramabana-tick', path='', limit=600), '/x/ramabana-tick --quiet --limit 600')
```

``` python
import contextlib, io, tempfile
from unittest.mock import patch as mpatch
def _tool(d, name, first='#!/bin/sh'): (f := Path(d)/name).write_text(first + '\n'); f.chmod(0o755)
if sys.platform != 'win32':
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    _tool(d, 'git'); _tool(d, 'claude', '#!/usr/bin/env node')
    test_eq(beat_missing(d, Path(d)/'ramabana-tick'), ['claude', 'git-lfs', str(Path(d)/'ramabana-tick')])   # claude needs node on the same PATH
    _tool(d, 'node'); _tool(d, 'git-lfs'); _tool(d, 'ramabana-tick')
    test_eq(beat_missing(d, Path(d)/'ramabana-tick'), [])
    class _hb:
        def __init__(self, script=None): self.script, self.cmd = script, None
        def install(self, cmd, tag, every): self.cmd = cmd; return Path(d)/'ramabana.sh'
        def installed(self, tag): return self.script
    hb, err = _hb(), io.StringIO()
    with mpatch.dict(os.environ, PATH=tempfile.mkdtemp()), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err), contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
        was, heartbeat = heartbeat, (lambda: hb)   # `tick` looks the scheduler up here
        try: test_eq(tick.__wrapped__(install=True, limit=900), 0)
        finally: heartbeat = was
    assert 'claude' in err.getvalue() and 'git-lfs' in err.getvalue(), err.getvalue()
    assert hb.cmd.endswith('--quiet --limit 900'), hb.cmd
```

``` python
if sys.platform != 'win32':
    old, new = Path(d)/'old.sh', Path(d)/'new.sh'
    old.write_text(f"#!/bin/sh\nexec '{d}/ramabana-tick' --quiet >> \"{d}/ramabana.log\" 2>&1\n")
    test_eq(_launcher(old.read_text()), (None, f'{d}/ramabana-tick'))
    with mpatch.dict(os.environ, RAMABANA_CONFIG=f'{d}/cfg/config.toml'):
        test_eq(beat_problems(_hb()), [])
        test_eq(len(beat_problems(_hb(str(old)))), 1)
        bare = tempfile.mkdtemp(); _tool(bare, 'git')
        new.write_text(f"#!/bin/sh\nexec /usr/bin/env PATH={bare} '{d}/gone/ramabana-tick' --quiet >> \"{d}/ramabana.log\" 2>&1\n")
        with mpatch.dict(os.environ, PATH=d): got = beat_problems(_hb(str(new)))
        test_eq(len(got), 2)
        assert 'claude' in got[0] and 'git-lfs' in got[0], got[0]
        assert 'gone/ramabana-tick, which is gone' in got[1]
        (Path(d)/'cfg').mkdir(); env = Path(d)/'cfg'/BEAT_ENV
        env.write_text('# keys for the beat\nexport RB_DEMO_KEY=from-file\nRB_DEMO_SET=from-file\n'); env.chmod(0o600)
        with mpatch.dict(os.environ, RB_DEMO_SET='from-shell'):
            test_eq(load_beat_env(), ['RB_DEMO_KEY'])
            test_eq((os.environ['RB_DEMO_KEY'], os.environ['RB_DEMO_SET']), ('from-file', 'from-shell'))
        env.chmod(0o644)
        with contextlib.redirect_stderr(io.StringIO()): test_eq(load_beat_env(), [])
        assert 'RB_DEMO_KEY' not in os.environ
        test_eq(len(beat_problems(_hb())), 1)
```

The example registers a schedule named `demo` that fires every second.
It waits for the schedule to come due and runs one beat against a
database in a temporary folder. The callback’s return value becomes the
note that
[`beat_notes`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#beat_notes)
reads back.

``` python
import contextlib, io, tempfile, time

@on_tick('demo')
def _demo(fire): return 'the beat ran this'

db = str(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'pob.db')
pob(db).add('demo', every='1s')
time.sleep(1.2)
out = io.StringIO()
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out): test_eq(tick.__wrapped__(db=db), 0)
test_eq(beat_notes(pob(db)), ['demo: the beat ran this'])
del TICKS['demo']
```

``` python
import subprocess, textwrap
db = str(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'pob.db')
pob(db).add('stuck', every='1s', retries=1)
time.sleep(1.2)
beat = textwrap.dedent(f"""
    import time
    from ramabana.monitor import on_tick, tick
    on_tick('stuck')(lambda fire: time.sleep(30))
    raise SystemExit(tick.__wrapped__(db={db!r}, limit=1))""")   # a process of its own: signals reach only the main thread
t = time.monotonic()
r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-c', beat], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
assert time.monotonic() - t < 20 and r.returncode == 0, r
test_eq(beat_notes(pob(db)), ['stuck: gave up after 1 tries. BeatTimeout: the beat ran past its 1s limit'])
got = []
_watchdog(0.1, exit=got.append); time.sleep(0.3)
test_eq(got, [124])
_watchdog(0.1, exit=got.append).cancel(); time.sleep(0.3)
test_eq(got, [124])
```

    the beat was still running after 0s; exiting

Notes can also be written straight to the database with
`note(title, body)`. A note with an empty body reads as its title alone:

``` python
import tempfile
beat = pob(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'pob.db')
beat.note('watches', '2 of 5 fired')
beat.note('nightly', '')
beat_notes(beat)
```

    ['watches: 2 of 5 fired', 'nightly']

After a reader drains the notes, it gets nothing more. Another reader
still sees all of them.
[`beat_notes`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#beat_notes)
returns an empty list when there is no database or when reading it
fails. A locked database never stops a turn.

``` python
test_eq(beat_notes(beat), [])
test_eq(beat_notes(beat, reader='another'), ['watches: 2 of 5 fired', 'nightly'])
test_eq(beat_notes(None), [])

class _Broken:
    def drain(self, reader, limit=20): raise RuntimeError('the database is locked')
test_eq(beat_notes(_Broken()), [])
```

A new reader starts at the first note. A session must not, or it shows
the notes of jobs that ended days ago.
[`beat_join`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#beat_join)
starts a reader that has never read at the newest note, so it sees only
the notes made after it joined. A reader that has read keeps its place.

``` python
beat.note('dhrona', 'ran')
beat_join(beat, 'late'); beat_join(beat, 'another')
test_eq(beat_notes(beat, reader='late'), [])
test_eq(beat_notes(beat, reader='another'), ['dhrona: ran'])
beat.note('abhyasa', 'indexed')
beat_join(beat, 'late')
test_eq(beat_notes(beat, reader='late'), ['abhyasa: indexed'])
beat_join(None, 'late'); beat_join(_Broken(), 'late')
```
